fr:mainmatter.html:p: I often use my ipad pro to take handwritten notes, and I find it frustrating that digital handwritten notes don't interagte with my other knowledge management in Forester. I think that is a real point of frustration, as there is a significant cognitive friction managing two independent systems. So I often give up and just use one or none of them.
We may wish to use OCR on notes as a hook when saving them, or perhaps as a nightly task. I don't know how effective that might be.

Maybe something as simple as a capturing workflow where I can easily link to a digital handwritten note from within a normal tree. Then on each device we can register a program that opens a notetaking app of choice for handling handwritten notes. And maybe we can the ability to link to digital notes from handwritten ones as well, and the OCR could detect this?
Merged into ForesterPad: iPad App Redesign.

Retired 2026-04-16. Replaced by Notes/Notability → capture endpoint on macproseph (see Forest Sync and Capture Architecture). The custom iPad client isn't worth maintaining when a share-sheet Shortcut into /capture covers the same ingest flow with a fraction of the code. Existing handwriting trees (hwn-* and the notebook-app=forester-pad meta) are preserved as-is.
Original design below is kept for historical reference.
Redesign ForesterPad from a handwriting-focused notes app into a touch-first forest client. Derived from design notes in Handwriting .
Bridge treeId sync bug: The server's data directory is missing most notes, so the bridge can't assign treeIds back to the iPad. Debug why only 2 of ~15 notes are in the server's data dir.
PencilKit toolbar activation: Double-tap eraser doesn't work on note switch. PKToolPicker not becoming active for the new first responder.
Claude skill for handwritten trees: Define a skill that reads a handwritten tree's PDF and transcribes it.
Emacs todo keybinding: Elisp function to create a TODO tree and insert a transclusion link at point.
Apple Vision OCR: Run VNRecognizeTextRequest on-device after save, store OCR text, bridge writes \meta{ocr-text} to the tree file. Enables full-text search of handwritten notes.

Flexible metadata/taxonomy: Remove hardcoded Handwriting taxon. Add a metadata editor panel in the app. Handwritten-ness should be a tag, not a taxon. Trees routing to PDFs should support arbitrary metadata, digital text, and mixed content.
Custom toolbar actions: Overlay forest-specific buttons alongside PencilKit toolbar (create todo, insert transclusion, set taxon). Equivalent to Emacs forest functions but for touch.
Full forest on iPad: The app should maintain a local copy of the entire forest, not just handwritten notes. Treat iPad and laptop uniformly. Bidirectional sync of all trees.
Canvas as element, not note: A handwritten canvas should be an element within a tree, not the entirety of it. Trees can mix canvas regions with digital text, transclusions, and queries.

Forest-as-notebook UI: Replace the flat note list with a rendered, navigable forest. Swipe for forward/back, touch-first interaction, inline canvas editing, visible metadata panel, context and backlinks accessible from within the app.
